To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the double pulse resistance spot welding of a TBF steel with a 1200 MPa minimum tensile strength leads to a ferritic-martensitic microstructures in the inner part of the weld nugget and to a fully tempered martensitic microstructure if the first pulse is chosen to be high enough to avoid splashing but low enough not to reaustenite the weld nugget.
the second pulse can be used to tailor the microstructure and the hardness of the welds.
a second pulse following a low current first pulse leads to reaustenization and a harder inner weld nugget.

a new approach to improve the mechanical properties of AHSS weld nuggets via double pulse resistance spot welding and the resulting microstructural evolution.

The main takeaway from our work is that
double pulse welding is not a panacea for improving the mechanical properties of spot welds of AHSS, but it can be used to produce welds with a microstructure that is harder than the parent material.
the second pulse is not a panacea for improving the mechanical performance of resistance spot welds in AHSS.
the first pulse is crucial for the microstructural evolution during the second pulse.
